FROMLIST: loop: Better discard support for block devices If the backing device for a loop device is a block device, then mirror the "write zeroes" capabilities of the underlying block device into the loop device. Copy this capability into both max_write_zeroes_sectors and max_discard_sectors of the loop device. The reason for this is that REQ_OP_DISCARD on a loop device translates into blkdev_issue_zeroout(), rather than blkdev_issue_discard(). This presents a consistent interface for loop devices (that discarded data is zeroed), regardless of the backing device type of the loop device. There should be no behavior change for loop devices backed by regular files. While in there, differentiate between REQ_OP_DISCARD and REQ_OP_WRITE_ZEROES, which are different for block devices, but which the loop device had just been lumping together, since they're largely the same for files. This change fixes blktest block/003, and removes an extraneous error print in block/013 when testing on a loop device backed by a block device that does not support discard. power: Refactor: Simplify dark resume logic. dark resume logic when written was expected to run on 3.8 kernel. 3.8 kernel did not have support for CLOCK_REALTIME_ALARM and CLOCK_BOOTTIME_ALARM. As a result dark resume logic when need to sleep for certain time have to pound on /dev/rtc directly to schedule a wakeup. As we are not planning to run dark resume on older kernels, we can simply instantiate SimpleAlarmTimer in dark_resume.cc if needed. So let us not pass the suspend duration to suspender anymore. There is one more reason for this refactor. SimpleAlarmTimer in the backend use timerfd_* API. timerfd_* allow the kernel to manage a list of events and have it program the RTC so the alarm will trigger for the earliest event in the list. This avoids the need for user space applications to coordinate in order to share the hardware. For timerfd_* to work properly, no user daemon should touch /dev/rtc directly. But any suspend_duration passed to suspender will result in a write to /dev/rtc. So let us not do that. CHROMIUM: cros_ec: use ODR events to clear the spreading history This uses the ODR flag introduced in CL:1450288 to clear the last batch data used by the spreading algorithm. The spreading code relies on accurately measuring the effective interval between batches of samples. An ODR change means that the previous batches may no longer represent the behavior of the EC. If an ODR change is immediately followed by a batch, the AP will attempt to spread based on the previous interval, which can easily lead to "spreading into the future", leading to subsequent timestamp mismatch errors. This patch solves that problem by having ODR events be breaking points for the spreading code. The tradeoff is that this can cause samples to be lost immediately after an ODR change. This problem can't effectively be solved without either: - storing those samples in a side queue and spreading them once updated information becomes available to do so; - communicating the ODR to the AP as part of the ODR event. Notes: 1) do not use ODR change and FLUSH events as input to the filter; these events come asynchronously to the regular flow of data, and including them in the filter history as the potential to disrupt the slope calculation; 2) clear the previous batch as well as the current on an ODR change; it is theoretically possible for us to reopen an old batch after an ODR change which would not work for the same reason reopening the current batch would not work. CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: Fix broken ble re-advertisement feature BLE advertisment needs to be re-enabled in kernel when previous ble connection goes away. This feature is broken from the commit 5084500d59bb ("CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: Remove the assumption on the Adv state in connection event") in 11/2017, this feature is broken in cros kernel 3.10, 3.14, 3.18 and 4.4. I have verified this feature using several linux kernels, including 4.19.25 in raspi 3 + ble dongle, and confirm ble advertisment needs to be re-enabled in __hci_req_schedule_adv_instance from kernel bluetooth when previous BLE connection goes away. Confirm with Luiz Augusto von Denz from bluetooth upstream, BLE advertisement needs to be re-enabled by kernel when previous BLE connection goes away, this feature has been there in bluetooth kernel upstream for several years. The code logic is roughly as below. When BLE connection is established, HCI_LE_ADV flag needs to be cleared via hci_dev_clear_flag(hdev, HCI_LE_ADV) in hci_le_conn_complete_evt, Linux bluetooth use this flag to check if advertisment is there. a. When there is no ble connection and ble advertisment is there, __hci_req_schedule_adv_instance is peridically called, and if that is just rescheduling the same instance, it does not execute any HCI command, and return since HCI_LE_ADV has been set, and it use same adv instance. b. When ble connection is established, HCI_LE_ADV flag is cleared in hci_le_conn_complete_evt. Then __hci_req_schedule_adv_instance would be periodically called, and it would goes to __hci_req_enable_advertising and does not enable advertisement since connection is there. c. When ble disconnection happens, when __hci_req_schedule_adv_instance is called again, it found HCI_LE_ADV has been cleared in b, and goes to call __hci_req_enable_advertising, and found ble connection is not there, and re-enable ble advertisement. Regarding the chromium:776423, it seems the previous fix is not right, it should be addressed by the below ways a.by the controller, fix Connection Failed to be Established issues. b.in kernel side, from hci_cs_le_read_remote_features() of hci_event.c, when the return status is not successful, setting LE advertising flag to true if it is cleared in hci_le_conn_complete_evt() previously in a connection attempt. c.Add "LE Set Advertise Enable" command with 0x00 (disabled) before the next "LE Set Advertising Parameters" command when hitting the error on LE read remote used features command. Either way, it should not break the ble re-advertisment feature. Revert "CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: Remove the assumption on the Adv state in connection event" This reverts commit 5084500d59bb4e09b01d5323323b2cf7e0758611. power: Manipulate wake mask during s0ix timeouts When S0ix failure detection is enabled and a timeout occurs such that the SLP_S0 line never actually toggles, then s0ix_transition_timeout() sets the HANG_DETECT event bit. This doesn't quite work in this scenario, since the wake mask is only enabled when the power state transitions to S0ix, which happens when the SLP_S0 line toggles. So the AP never sees the event, since it's not in the wake mask and so never causes the EC->AP interrupt line to change. Detect this situation in the timeout function, and explicitly move the wake mask to its S0ix value so that when the event bit is set, (if it is in the wake mask), the system will wake up. Doing this forcefully gets the wake mask out of sync with the power state. So upon resume, explicitly restore the wake mask to its S0 state. BUG=b:131434497 BRANCH=none TEST=suspend_stress_test -c1 --suspend_min=60 with a firmware where S0ix fails.
